findings.detail: Current 'Desactivado pausa las actualizaciones de todos los vínculos de agentes/habilidades; activado suscribe los nuevos.' is 113 cells against the sidecar's declared maxCells 72, which settings_io.py:5121 restates in code ('Help strings are budgeted to <=72 cells (the detail line at 100 columns)'). The row is section 'hub' (settings_io.py:5120-5133). settings_view.py:4767 sets bridge_row only when section == team_bridge.BRIDGE_SECTION, and BRIDGE_SECTION is the literal 'team_bridge' (team_bridge/availability.py:33); the wrap rung exists only inside the bridge_row branches (settings_view.py:4837 comment 'A ``None`` rung is the WRAP slot (bridge rows only)', created at 4881, consumed at 4910 by _wrap_cells). A hub row therefore falls to the ladder whose last rung is settings_view.py:4937, a marked truncation. Measured: the string is cut at 98 cells on a 100-column terminal and at 78 on an 80-column one, and fits whole only from 115 columns. What is cut is 'activado suscribe los nuevos' - the ON behaviour, i.e. the half that says what turning the switch on does.
findings.remediation: 'Desactivado pausa todas las actualizaciones; activado suscribe nuevas.' (70 cells, measured) - keeps the 'all' ceiling and both halves inside 72; the row's own on/off descriptions already spell out 'vínculos de agentes y habilidades'. This is round-1 es-w1-A02's proposal and it is still the right fix.

findings.detail: Current 'Predeterminado para nuevos vínculos de equipo; los existentes conservan sus propias políticas.' is 94 cells against the same declared maxCells 72. It fits the 98-cell detail band at 100 columns once the key path sheds, and truncates at 80 columns (78 cells), losing 'propias políticas'. So unlike C03 this is a narrow-width limit rather than an always-cut string. NOTE: on the current wiring this key never renders at all - see the source_notes - so the width defect is latent rather than visible today.
findings.remediation: 'Predeterminado para vínculos nuevos; los existentes conservan la suya.' (70 cells, measured).

findings.detail: Round 1's clip was fixed by inventing an abbreviation: 'Autoactualizar agentes/habil.' is 29 cells and no longer truncates, but 'habil.' is not a Spanish abbreviation of 'habilidad' and the label now reads unlike its sibling 'Suscribir vínculos de equipo', which keeps the full noun. The English keeps the same shape on both rows ('Auto-update agent/skill links', 'Subscribe new team links'), and 'links' is absent from the Spanish label although the help and both descriptions use 'vínculos'. Meaning stays recoverable (the switch does auto-update the agents' content).
findings.remediation: 'Vínculos de agente/habilidad' (28 cells, measured) - a noun label like its sibling, no invented abbreviation, and 'vínculos' comes back; or round-1's 'Autoactualizar vínculos' (23) if the verb must stay.

findings.detail: One English term, three Spanish renderings across the locale: 'vínculo' for a hub subscription link (all eight link-bearing keys here), 'enlace' for a hyperlink (tui.notifications.section_links 'Enlaces', relay.notifications.detail.section.links 'Enlaces', wire.slash.links 'Abre un enlace de esta conversación en el navegador'), and wire.slash.hub left in English entirely ('Open Hub links — per-link subscribe and auto-push policy'). Neither i18n/glossary.md nor i18n/style-guides/es.md records a row for 'link'. The sense split (subscription relationship vs hyperlink) is defensible, which is why this is minor, but an unrecorded three-way split is drift rather than a decision. Round-1 es-w1-A04, unchanged.
findings.remediation: Record the row in i18n/style-guides/es.md: hub link -> 'vínculo', browser hyperlink -> 'enlace', and settle wire.slash.hub when that namespace is audited.

source_notes.text: FIVE OF NINE KEYS HAVE NO LIVE CONSUMER. wire_settings_hub_defaults is imported once (settings_io.py:72) and only agents_label, agents_on_description, agents_off_description and agents_help are called (_hd. sites: 5126, 5130, 5131, 5133). The teams row is registered with wire.settings keys instead: settings_io.py:5139 label=_t(_ws.hub_auto_update_teams_label()), 5142/5143 its choice descriptions, 5145 its help. So teams.label, teams.help, teams.on.description, teams.off.description and model_default.note are translated, hashed and shipped in the catalogue but render nowhere in this repository. Consequence for round 2: the round-1 nit that shortened teams.label from 35 to 28 cells (es-w1-A05) fixed copy that nothing displays, and C04's width defect is latent. Recorded as a source-side fact, not as a defect in the Spanish.

The sidecar declares maxCells 72 on exactly the two help keys and on no label, although both labels are rendered through the 29-cell truncation. Combined with the wiring note, the budget the translator was given (72) is the one the code comment states, and the label budget they were not given (29) is the one that produced round 1's clip and this round's abbreviation (C05).

help_width_note.text: Both help strings remain over the declared 72 cells and this audit records both as findings, not as accepted limits. agents.help (113 cells) is a REAL DEFECT at every terminal size below 115 columns, including the 100-column width the code comment budgets for: the hub section has no wrap rung, so the sentence is cut mid-clause with a visible ellipsis and loses 'activado suscribe los nuevos'. teams.help (94 cells) is a narrow-width limit only (fits at 100 columns after the key path sheds, truncates at 80), and it is latent because the key is unwired. The briefing's reasoning that the wrap rung saves them is refuted above.

fact_1_label_budget.claim: every settings row label is rendered as truncate_cells(label, 29)
fact_1_label_budget.evidence: settings_view.py:4020 truncate_cells(setting.label, _LABEL_BUDGET); settings_view.py:434 _LABEL_BUDGET = _VALUE_COLUMN(34) - _ROW_INDENT(2) - _MARKER_WIDTH(2) - 1 = 29; truncate_cells cannot wrap (tool_card.py:728-750).
fact_1_label_budget.consequence: Any label over 29 cells is painted cut with a visible ellipsis. Applies to the console rows (settings_io.py:4774-4799, section 'console', always visible) and to the hub and failover rows, not only to the two namespaces the briefing named.

fact_2_wrap_rung.claim_as_briefed: when no rung fits, _wrap_cells(help_text, width, max_lines=2) renders the help across two rows, so the two hub_defaults help strings are acceptable with a narrow-width limit
fact_2_wrap_rung.evidence: The wrap rung is a None entry in the shed ladder and is created only in the bridge_row branches (settings_view.py:4881 for the no-clause case, 4873 region for the clause case). bridge_row is set at settings_view.py:4767 from section == team_bridge.BRIDGE_SECTION, and BRIDGE_SECTION is the literal 'team_bridge' (team_bridge/availability.py:33). The hub rows are section 'hub' (settings_io.py:5120). No None rung exists for them, so _wrap_cells at 4910 is never reached and the ladder's last rung, settings_view.py:4937, applies: truncate_cells(rendered.plain, width) - a marked cut, not a wrap. _wrap_cells' own docstring scopes it to 'the agent-messages explanation only'.
fact_2_wrap_rung.measured: _detail_width() is max(total-2, 24) (settings_view.py:5203), i.e. 98 cells at 100 columns and 78 at 80. agents.help is 113 cells -> truncated at both sizes, whole only from 115 columns. teams.help is 94 -> whole at 100 columns once the key path sheds, truncated at 80.
fact_2_wrap_rung.consequence: The briefing's premise is wrong for this surface; round 1 had it right. agents.help is a real defect (C03 major), not an accepted narrow-width limit. teams.help is a narrow-width limit only (C04 minor).
